I analyzed the saved Oct. 11 batch, [“luna-18-tests” results](</Users/juri/ai-agent-tacto/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/tactika-buyer-agent/runs/luna-18-tests-20261011/results-20261011T043504Z-4f0d8066.json>). **The agent completed all 10 cases and made 9 deals, but averaged 44.12% on the Arena score.** That suggests deal completion is much stronger than deal quality.

### Main weaknesses

1. **It sometimes accepts too early.** In P02, it accepted the opening €370.96 offer without countering and scored **0**. The planner’s own target cost was higher than that offer, so its target calculation treated the opening price as good even though it captured none of the scored savings. [P02 trace](</Users/juri/ai-agent-tacto/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/tactika-buyer-agent/runs/luna-18-tests-20261011/case_P02-e075eb37aafdb7d1-e93f4231.json>)

2. **Several deals leave much of the available savings uncaptured.** P05 scored **20.6%**, P18 **31.9%**, and P07 **44.2%**. P03, by comparison, scored **90.0%**. The results point to uneven target setting and negotiation performance across cases.

3. **It repeats itself when a supplier does not move.** In P11, the first three buyer proposals were identical while the supplier repeated its €48.50 counter. That used three turns without changing the offer. [P11 trace](</Users/juri/ai-agent-tacto/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/tactika-buyer-agent/runs/luna-18-tests-20261011/case_P11-e87dd3d246b038e2-bd237a1a.json>)

4. **It accepts costly index exposure in some deals.** P08 and P18 ended with index clauses using a 45% material share and zero deadband. The cost breakdown includes about **€31.8k** in index cost and risk for P08, and **€8.4k** for P18. The cost model accounts for this exposure, but these deals still scored only 57.1% and 31.9%.

5. **The council did not contribute usable advice in this batch.** All 24 proposal decisions were recorded as `specialist_fallback`; there were no rejection forecasts to score. The saved results don’t show why specialist responses fell back, so I can’t tell whether the cause was API responses, validation, or timeouts.

P04 ended without a deal: the supplier’s final quote cost more than the planner’s fallback supply, so walking away was consistent with its BATNA rule, but the case scored 0. That looks like a real trade-off between protecting cost and securing a deal, rather than an obvious protocol failure.

The replay found **no decision divergences**, and there were no recorded run failures. That supports repeatability, not negotiation quality. The sample is only 10 cases, with no paired deterministic-versus-council comparison, so it can’t establish whether Luna improved results.

Skipped: I didn’t rerun tests or make live Arena calls. Risk: this is one small batch, so the weaknesses are signals to investigate, not a reliable estimate of performance across all cases.
